items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I had this little band I put together, with Buddy Childress... Arnold Ross was in that band and Paul Sarmento and Buddy Childress

ctx.x: played around some terrible joints. I had to step over a dead body in one joint to get out the back door. I mean I didn't know he was dead at the time. I thought he was drunk and asleep. I found out the next day he'd been shot there. And I finally wound up in -- it was out here. I worked out in California with the big band, doing some dates around locally, playing weekends and things like that. And then I went back to the little band after that. And after a couple of scenes, like I said, stepping over this guy,…

I wasn't you know, but he was very jealous and drunk all the time, and he thought something was going on, and what was going on was she'd had it with him and he was looking to blame anybody he could blame. So I got out of that scene. And I had this little band I put together, with Buddy Childress, like I told you. We came back and we played the El Rancho and some other places, and we went up to Alaska. We were up there for two weeks, up in Anchorage. And if I'd have stayed up there another week I think I'd have…

was in that band and Paul Sarmento and Buddy Childress, and Boone Stines was the drummer, a guy out of Oklahoma, a guy that had a good beat but no technique. And then I -- this guy at MCA, Bob Wooling, said, "Look, you shouldn't be fooling around with this gig. Why don't you play the Palladium." I said, "They won't let me in with a mixed band." He said, "You don't have a mixed band. You don't have any band. What are you talking about?"
